newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar falls through supports, seen lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar falls through supports, seen lower.

text.p: The dollar fell through substantial supports on Friday as broad-based dollar weakness continued and technical analysts said the dollar will move even lower, toward trendline support, versus the mark and yen.
Dollar/yen broke support at 111.80 yen in early trade and will likely break trendline support at 111.25 in an effort to hit its short-term target of 109.70/75, technicians said.
The weekly trendline was formed from connecting the August 1996 lows, said John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.
"I think that (111.25 dollar/yen) is where we are gong to be heading. We didn't even have any upside today," Tirone said.
Below the trendline, dollar/yen support lies at the 111 and 110 figures.

Another analyst at a U.S. investment bank said the dollar would have to break resistance at 112.80 and 113.20 yen plus trade above that level on a regular basis before a retest of the October 29 high of 114.92 yen could occur.
Against the mark, Tirone traced a long-term weekly trendline, connecting October 1995 and August 1996 lows, that suggests dollar/mark will fall to 1.4930 soon.
A move above a barrier at 1.5270 marks and especially through key resistance at 1.5330 would be a bullish signal, analysts said.
Dollar/mark support was quoted at 1.5010 and 1.4960.
The dollar opened at 1.5107/10 marks and 111.83/88 yen and inched down to 1.5025/35 marks and 111.57/62 yen by 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
